title: ACA s. 34 — Application for setting aside arbitral award

content.overview: Section 34 provides the exclusive recourse against an arbitral award under Part I on the limited grounds set out in the section, including incapacity, invalid arbitration agreement, lack of proper notice or opportunity, excess of mandate, improper composition or procedure, non-arbitrability, and conflict with the public policy of India. For domestic awards, patent illegality appearing on the face of the award is an additional ground under section 34(2A). The court may set aside the award or, in limited circumstances, adjourn under section 34(4); it does not modify the award.
content.glance: Limited set-aside grounds under s. 34; patent illegality for domestic awards only; no power to modify the award (Hakeem).
content.study: Section 34 is the exclusive Part I challenge route. Post-2015 public policy is narrowed; patent illegality under s. 34(2A) applies only to domestic awards and must go to the root of the matter. Courts cannot modify awards under s. 34.

sections.heading: Grounds for setting aside
sections.body: The grounds in section 34(2) and, for domestic awards, patent illegality under section 34(2A).

sections.heading: Public policy and patent illegality
sections.body: Public policy is construed narrowly after the 2015 Amendment; patent illegality must appear on the face of the award and go to the root of the matter.

sections.heading: No modification
sections.body: Section 34 confers a power to set aside (or limited remission under s. 34(4)), not to modify the award.

provisions.title: Application for setting aside arbitral award

cases.name: Ssangyong Engineering & Construction Co. Ltd. v. NHAI
cases.facts: Challenge to a domestic award on public policy and patent illegality grounds after the 2015 amendments.
cases.issue: Scope of public policy of India and patent illegality under section 34 after the 2015 Amendment.
cases.ratioDecidendi: Public policy is narrowed; patent illegality under s. 34(2A) must go to the root of the matter and does not cover mere erroneous application of law. Patent illegality is available only for domestic awards.
cases.holding: Clarified the narrowed post-2015 grounds for setting aside.
cases.relevance: Leading post-2015 authority on section 34 public policy and patent illegality.

cases.name: Project Director, NHAI v. M. Hakeem
cases.facts: High Courts had modified compensation awards under section 34 in National Highways matters.
cases.issue: Does section 34 empower a court to modify an arbitral award?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Section 34 confers only a power to set aside or to adjourn for remission under s. 34(4); it does not include a power to modify, revise or vary the award.
cases.holding: Courts cannot modify an arbitral award under section 34.
cases.relevance: Settles that the s. 34 remedy is limited to set-aside or limited remission, not modification.

cases.name: Associate Builders v. Delhi Development Authority
cases.facts: Challenge to an award on public policy and related grounds.
cases.issue: How should public policy of India under section 34 be understood?
cases.ratioDecidendi: Public policy includes fundamental policy of Indian law, interest of India, justice or morality, and patent illegality; judicial review is not appellate review of the merits.
cases.holding: Restated the contours of public policy; still cited for structure of review, read with Ssangyong for current law.
cases.relevance: Important authority on section 34; read with Ssangyong for post-2015 law.

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can a court modify an arbitral award under section 34?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: No. Project Director, NHAI v. M. Hakeem holds that section 34 does not include a power to modify the award; the court may set aside or, in limited cases, adjourn under section 34(4).
questionsAndAnswers.explanation: Settled by the Supreme Court in 2021.
